question: Does selecting training duration by inner-family generalization remedy the E150 memorization gap?
partition: Preserve E73 outer3fold. Inside each outer fitting partition, SHA256(E151-inner:seed) mod5==0 defines inner validation; all other fitting families train the inner model. Outer validation never participates in that choice. Descendants stay with their family.
selection: One inner run of2000 updates. Measure the family/stage/branch balanced within-state squared loss at0,25,50,100,250,500,1000,2000 steps. Select minimum loss, earlier exact ties. Step0 represents unchanged-parent scores. Do not use terminal win counts or outer outcomes to pick a step.
refit: Restart from the E150 initialization and train on all outer fitting families for the chosen number of updates. Full public features, learned one-scalar parent offset, optimizer, sampling and seeds match E150. Selecting2000 must reproduce the existing E150 tensors bit-for-bit. Save inner splits, complete loss curves, selection, final model and outer results.
evidence: E148/E150 training first-card results saturate their measured fit ceilings while outer families fail. This motivates a learning-curve test, not an established diagnosis that any particular shorter duration helps.
gate: Retain original screen: first_card and boss_then_card each gain20/1536 versus parent with descriptive paired p<.025. Compare with E150 fixed2000. No alternative loss metric, checkpoint grid expansion, outer threshold tuning or automatic adoption.
limits: These historical-family folds are development data. Nested selection protects outer labels within this experiment but does not erase prior study exposure. Recorded scopes do not measure a complete repeatedly changed natural policy or final50% unseen acceptance. No new games or sampling.
